Relationships between components

Define and use relationships between components

Sometimes it is necessary to implement a component like this:

<custom-ul>
  <custom-li> item 1 </custom-li>
  <custom-li> item 2 </custom-li>
</custom-ul>

In this example, custom-ul and custom-li are both custom components. They have relationships with each other, and the communication between them is often complicated. At this time, adding the relations definition section when defining the component can solve this problem. Example:

// path/to/custom-ul.js
Component({
  relations: {
    '../custom-li/custom-li': {
      type: 'child', // The associated target node should be a child node.
      linked: function (target) {
        // Executed every time a custom-li is inserted, the target is the node instance object, and is triggered after the attached life cycle of the node.
        console.log("---linked---")
      },
      linkChanged: function (target) {
        // It is executed every time a custom-li is moved. The target is the node instance object and is triggered after the node's moved life cycle.
        console.log("---linkChanged---")
      },
      unlinked: function (target) {
        // Executed every time a custom-li is removed, the target is the node instance object, and is triggered after the detached life cycle of the node.
        console.log("---unlinked---")
      }
    }
  },
  methods: {
    _getAllLi: function () {
      // Use getRelationNodes to get the nodes array, which contains all associated custom-li and is ordered.
      var nodes = this.getRelationNodes('../custom-li/custom-li')
      console.log(nodes)
    }
  },
  ready: function () {
    this._getAllLi()
  },
})

// path/to/custom-li.js
Component({ 
  relations: {
    '../custom-ul/custom-ul': {
      type: 'parent', // The associated target node should be the parent node.
      linked: function (target) {
        // Executed every time it is inserted into custom-ul. The target is the custom-ul node instance object, which is triggered after the attached life cycle.
        console.log("---linked---")
      },
      linkChanged: function (target) {
        // Executed every time it is moved. The target is the custom-ul node instance object, which is triggered after the moved life cycle.        
        console.log("---linkChanged---")
      },
      unlinked: function (target) {
        // Executed every time it is removed, the target is the custom-ul node instance object, triggered after the detached life cycle.
        console.log("---unlinked---")
      }
    }
  }
})

Note: relations definitions must be added to both component definitions, otherwise they will not take effect.

Associate a series of components

Sometimes, what needs to be associated is a type of component, such as:

<custom-form>
  <view>
    input
    <custom-input></custom-input>
  </view>
  <custom-submit> submit </custom-submit>
</custom-form>

The custom-form component wants to associate the two components custom-input and custom-submit. At this point, if both components have the same behavior:

// path/to/custom-form-controls.js
module.exports = Behavior({
  attached: function () {
    console.log("Behavior attached");
  },
});

// path/to/custom-input.js
var customFormControls = require('./custom-form-controls')
Component({
  behaviors: [customFormControls],
  relations: {
    './custom-form': {
      type: 'ancestor', // The associated target node should be an ancestor node.
    }
  }
})

// path/to/custom-submit.js
var customFormControls = require('./custom-form-controls')
Component({
  behaviors: [customFormControls],
  relations: {
    './custom-form': {
      type: 'ancestor', // The associated target node should be an ancestor node.
    }
  }
})

Then in the relations relationship definition, you can use this behavior instead of the component path as the associated target node:

// path/to/custom-form.js
var customFormControls = require('./custom-form-controls')
Component({
  relations: {
    'customFormControls': {
      type: 'descendant', // The associated target node should be a descendant node
      target: customFormControls,
      linked: function(target) {
        console.info('Already linked to ' + target.is)
      }
    }
  }
})

relations definition section

The relations definition section contains the target component path and its corresponding options. The options that can be included are shown in the table below.

Options Type Required Description
type String YES The relative relationship of the target component, the optional values ​​are parent , child , ancestor , descendant
linked Function NO The relationship life cycle function is triggered when the relationship is established in the page node tree. The triggering time is after the component attached life cycle.
linkChanged Function NO The relationship life cycle function is triggered when the relationship changes in the page node tree. The triggering time is after the component moved life cycle.
unlinked Function NO The relationship life cycle function is triggered when the relationship leaves the page node tree. The triggering time is after the component's detached life cycle.
target String NO If this item is set, it represents the behavior that the associated target node should have, and all component nodes with this behavior will be associated.
